introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation

$$x\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y.$$
incertitudes: Question 3 (ii) : le sujet ne donne que y = 0 pour x = 1 et ne précise pas comment obtenir la deuxième valeur y_1 (x = 1,2) dont la formule à trois niveaux a besoin. Le corrigé la calcule par la méthode d'Euler (y_1 = 0,2) et obtient 0,7333 ; il note que la solution exacte y = x ln x donne 0,7520 et que partir de la valeur exacte y_1 = 0,2188 donnerait 0,7539. La valeur finale dépend donc du choix du départ, qui n'est pas imprimé.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the approximation $2h\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_n \cong y_{n+1} - y_{n-1}$ to show that

$$y_{n+1} \cong y_{n-1} + 2h\left(1 + \frac{y_n}{x_n}\right). \quad \textit{[2 marks]}$$
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dividing the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y$ by $x$ gives

$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \frac{y}{x}.$$

At the point $(x_n, y_n)$ this reads $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_n = 1 + \dfrac{y_n}{x_n}$. Substituting into the given approximation $2h\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_n \cong y_{n+1} - y_{n-1}$:

$$y_{n+1} - y_{n-1} \cong 2h\left(1 + \frac{y_n}{x_n}\right) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad y_{n+1} \cong y_{n-1} + 2h\left(1 + \frac{y_n}{x_n}\right). \qquad \blacksquare$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $y = 0$ when $x = 1$, estimate, using a step-length of $0.2$, the value of $y$ when $x = 1.6$, giving your final answer to $4$ significant figures. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $h = 0.2$, so $x_0 = 1$, $x_1 = 1.2$, $x_2 = 1.4$, $x_3 = 1.6$, with $y_0 = 0$.

**Starting value.** The three-level formula needs $y_0$ and $y_1$. Only $y_0$ is given, so obtain $y_1$ from the Euler step $y_1 = y_0 + h\left(1 + \dfrac{y_0}{x_0}\right)$:

$$y_1 = 0 + 0.2\left(1 + \frac{0}{1}\right) = 0.2.$$

**Step to $x_2 = 1.4$** (formula with $n = 1$):

$$y_2 = y_0 + 2h\left(1 + \frac{y_1}{x_1}\right) = 0 + 0.4\left(1 + \frac{0.2}{1.2}\right) = 0.4 \times \frac{7}{6} = 0.46667.$$

**Step to $x_3 = 1.6$** (formula with $n = 2$):

$$y_3 = y_1 + 2h\left(1 + \frac{y_2}{x_2}\right) = 0.2 + 0.4\left(1 + \frac{0.46667}{1.4}\right) = 0.2 + 0.4 \times 1.33333 = 0.73333.$$

| $n$ | $x_n$ | $y_n$ |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1.0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1.2 | 0.2 (Euler starter) |
| 2 | 1.4 | 0.4667 |
| 3 | 1.6 | 0.7333 |

$$\boxed{y(1.6) \approx 0.7333}$$

**Check against the exact solution.** The equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x} = 1$ has integrating factor $\dfrac1x$, giving $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \dfrac1x$, so $y = x\ln x + Cx$; $y(1) = 0$ gives $C = 0$ and $y = x\ln x$. Then $y(1.6) = 1.6\ln 1.6 \approx 0.7520$. The estimate is slightly low because the starting value $y_1 = 0.2$ is less accurate than the exact $1.2\ln 1.2 \approx 0.2188$ (starting from the exact $y_1$ the same formula gives $0.7539$).
